readme: Per-exercise corrections applied on top of the deterministic mapping tables in
apps/api/src/exercises/ingest/mappings.ts, keyed by the source dataset's own id.
This file exists because a mapping table can only be as precise as the source
vocabulary allows. free-exercise-db has one 'cardio' category covering everything from
a treadmill run to a stairmaster, so a table can map it to exactly one canonical
category and one measure -- and will be wrong for the rest. Overrides fix the
individual rows without turning the table into a pile of special cases.
Rules: an override may only set 'category', 'goal' or 'measure'; a value outside the
canonical vocabulary in @forjd/domain is rejected; and an override naming a source id
the dataset does not contain is rejected rather than ignored, so a re-vendor that drops
an exercise fails loudly instead of leaving dead config behind. Every id here must also
have a golden-fixture assertion in free-exercise-db.adapter.spec.ts -- that too is
Adding one is a product decision, not a mechanical fix. Say why in this file.

running-split: The base table maps source category 'cardio' to canonical 'cross_training'. Four of
the fourteen cardio entries are literally running or walking, and the design's
exercise library draws a 'Running' filter chip. Without these four the chip would be
empty on a freshly ingested catalogue.
time-not-distance: The base table measures 'cardio' by distance, which is right for a treadmill, a bike
or a rower -- all of which report metres. It is wrong for a fixed-position machine or
for skipping, where the only thing a user logs is how long they kept going.
